scenarios.note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for residual left-sided hemiparesis.

HPI: Pt is an 85-year-old female presenting for follow-up of lingering deficits following a prior ischemic stroke. Pt reports stable status but notes intermittent difficulty with fine motor tasks using her left side. She remains right-hand dominant and is able to perform most ADLs independently, though she requires some assistance with heavy lifting and dressing due to the left-sided hemiparesis. No new complaints of weakness or sensory changes reported since last visit.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Aspirin 81mg daily
- Meloxicam 15mg daily

Vitals:
BP: 138/82
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Weight: 142 lbs

Recent Labs:
HbA1c: 6.2%
eGFR: 68 mL/min/1.73m2
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
Lipid Panel: LDL 88, HDL 45, Trig 140

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, weight loss.
Neurological: Denies headache, dizziness, or vision changes.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or swelling.
Other: Denies shortness of breath or chest pain.

Social History: Retired. Lives at home with her daughter. No tobacco use. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Mother had hypertension and heart disease. Father had a history of myocardial infarction.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Well-groomed.
Neuro: Cranial nerves II-XII intact. Normal sensation to light touch throughout. Motor: 5/5 strength in right upper/lower extremities. 3/5 strength in left upper extremity; 4/5 strength in left lower extremity. Gait steady with a single-point cane.
Musculoskeletal: No joint swelling or erythema.

Assessment:
1. Residual left-sided hemiparesis from a prior ischemic stroke.
2. Hypertension.
3. Hyperlipidemia.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications.
2. Maintain current physical therapy regimen for left-sided hemiparesis.
3. Continue aspirin and statin for secondary prevention.
4. F/u in 3 months for routine check.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, DO
05/14/2026

Follow-up for residual right-sided hemiparesis.

She notes some difficulty with fine motor tasks due to right-sided hemiparesis but continues to perform ADLs with assistance. She remains right-handed. No new complaints of weakness or sensory changes reported since last visit.

Medication List
1. Lisinopril 10mg QD
2. Atorvastatin 20mg QD
3. Aspirin 81mg QD

Vitals
BP: 132/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht/Hgb: 34% / 10.2 g/dL
eGFR: 62 mL/min

Review of Systems
Negative for chest pain, SOB, syncope, or focal weakness. No changes in vision or hearing.

Social History
Lives at home with daughter. Retired. No tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, Stroke.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Neuro: Cranial nerves II-XII intact. Motor: 4/5 strength in right upper and lower extremities. Decreased sensation in right hand. Pt is right-hand dominant. Gait steady with a cane.
